subject: Trial orientation & deployment path — Medscribe pilot options
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Moroz <elena@medscribe.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Aug 2027 14:08:00 +0000
Subject: Trial orientation & deployment path — Medscribe pilot options

Hi Elena — thanks again for taking time today. Quick written recap and proposed next steps so we have everything captured.

Call highlights (short):
- Primary goal: validate inference latency and cost at 50k monthly requests for clinical summarization pipelines (PHI in scope).
- Constraints: HIPAA/BAA is required; company prefers data to remain in customer-controlled network if possible.
- Success metrics suggested by your team: p95 latency <120ms, <1.5¢ per inference (token-adjusted), no model quality regression on the 200-case eval set.

Deployment options we covered (tradeoffs):
1) Hosted API — fastest to ship; limited for PHI unless we layer redaction/bring-your-own-key and sign BAA. Good for initial functional testing (2–4 weeks).
2) Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) — isolated capacity on Redwood-managed infra. Can be BAA-backed and gives predictable throughput; faster than fully private but requires contract/commit. Good middle ground (4–8 week pilot).
3) Private VPC / on-prem connector — full network control, ideal for regulated PHI workflows; longer setup (network config, KMS, audit logs) typically 6–12 weeks.

Proposed trial orientations (pick one):
A) Short functional trial (Hosted + redaction): 3 weeks. Deliverable: integration guide, sample eval run, latency/cost baseline.
B) Dedicated pilot (reserved pool + BAA): 6 weeks. Deliverable: dedicated cluster, throughput tests, cost estimates, legal kickoff.
C) Private VPC pilot (network onboarding + compliance): 10 weeks. Deliverable: VPC peering / connector, SOC/BAA controls, end-to-end PHI demo.

Asks / next steps from Medscribe:
- Choose preferred orientation (A/B/C)
- Confirm technical leads (network/security + engineering) who can join kickoff — we noted Raj and Ana on the call but please confirm emails and roles.
- Procurement contact for SOW/BAA and target budget window.
- Proposed kickoff week (we suggested week of Aug 23).

I attached a short trial-charter-template and a network-questionnaire to speed the infra evaluation. If you prefer, we can start with option B (Dedicated) while we parallelize network questions for a later VPC move — that’s a common path.

I’ll await your preference and will draft a recommended schedule and resource list once you confirm orientation.

Best,
Naomi Feldman

Thanks Naomi — helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side:

- HIPAA is mandatory. We will need a signed BAA before any PHI leaves our network. If Dedicated comes with a BAA option and the ability to encrypt keys under our KMS, that will be acceptable for a pilot.
- Technical leads: Raj (Head of Platform, raj.patel@medscribe.ai) will be primary for infra/network; Ana (Lead ML Eng, ana.gomez@medscribe.ai) for model integration and evals.
- Procurement: procurement@medscribe.ai handles SOW and PO; we may need an initial cost estimate to secure internal approvals.
- Timeline: We prefer to start in the last week of Aug (week of 23rd) if legal review can move quickly.

Can you provide a one-page architecture sketch for the Dedicated option and a rough cost range (monthly) for a 1–2 month reserved pilot? If you think the VPC timeline will be longer than 10 weeks we should know that up front.

Elena
VP Product, Medscribe.ai

4) Implementation approach: recommend Dedicated pilot first (shorter setup) with explicit gating to move to Private VPC if network controls or latency SLAs aren’t met. That keeps momentum and buys time for contractual items.

Please mark these as done / blocked so I can track in the deal.
